items.content_html: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

items.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
items.content_html: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

items.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
items.content_html: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

items.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms

items.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
items.content_html: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

items.content_html: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

items.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
items.content_html: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

items.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
items.content_html: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

items.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
items.content_html: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.
